myths.title: La creación de la tierra y los Paretare
myths.entrada: Papá Grande, the elderly male creator, crouches at the left of a wide EMPTY sandy earth, adding one piece of clay to extend its edge like making a pot. No crops or trees yet. Large empty pale sky.
myths.acto: Papá Grande is above at a distant upper edge; Huhun Krukroring Merana, the first adult Ette man, descends feet first toward the San Ángel savanna after refusing to go. One suspended adult cutout, no impact, no wings, no modern parachute. Ground and lagoon far below; spacious tall scene.
myths.huella: A compact irregular terracotta earth slab being enlarged by one adjoining clay piece; two very small bare human footprints appear on the newly extended surface. Warm blank paper around it.
myths.limits: This is the clay / first-man version, NOT Yaau and Numirinta's maize creation. Footprints are an editorial metaphor, not an authentic emblem.

myths.title: Sol y Luna
myths.entrada: The younger female Sun and her older male brother Moon are separate human paper-cut figures in an open horizon at dawn, not lovers. Their reference identities are distinct. The woman Sun carries daylight through a plain cut-paper disk behind her, the brother Moon occupies the cooler side. Small full figures, much sky.
myths.acto: Show the change of solar ages as three broad layered horizons, one after another in depth: the first Sun's old western rising, the second beyond the Sierra Nevada, the present younger female Sun rising at the eastern open edge. A single current small female figure; the older horizons are light traces, not extra living Sun sisters.
myths.huella: Three broad cut-paper solar arcs of different lengths nested as a compact motif, with the present warm sun disk on the eastern edge and one cool crescent set apart for her older brother. Blank cream surrounding field.
myths.limits: Sun is FEMALE and Moon her older MALE brother. Three historical solar ages, not three suns shining together. Arcs are editorial visualization, not a traditional glyph.

myths.title: Las tres flechas del poblamiento
myths.entrada: A small group of newly arrived Ette adults pauses in a wet lowland forest opening, looking for a direction. Damp vegetation without a drinking vessel or feast. Off-center open path and much breathing space.
myths.acto: Papá Grande draws a broad softly colored rainbow as a bow. Exactly THREE straight maná-cane arrows leave toward three distinct far horizons, San Ángel, Cesar, Cartagena, no labels or literal modern cityscape. People follow the separate routes far behind.
myths.huella: Exactly three straight cane arrows diverge from one origin across three subtly folded earth-paper paths. Pale background, muted colors, no map border or geographic text.
myths.limits: Do not invent settlement dates, city founding, or rainbow ceremonial costume.

myths.title: Memoria de las primeras guerras
myths.entrada: An old milling stone rests prominently near the left forest path, testimony to an earlier Aruaco presence. Small Ette adult travelers approach in the distance, no identifiable fabricated Aruaco costume.
myths.acto: A restrained distant non-graphic confrontation and displacement on diverging forest paths: two small adult groups separated by a large empty clearing, held bows lowered or at their sides. No arrows hitting, no blood, no victorious hero.
myths.huella: One worn milling stone beside two separated cut-paper paths, one path receding into absence. Compact symbolic object composition on pale cream.
myths.limits: No exact ethnic costume for the other group can be inferred. No white-savior peace scene, maps, dates, or glorification.

myths.title: El diluvio, la lechuza y el totumo
myths.entrada: A vast muted blue flood covers the lowland forest. One high island carries a totumo tree with small karau bird and Nuti opossum sheltering high in its branches; the opossum hangs by its tail. No boat, no ark, no people outside.
myths.acto: Inside a simple round multilevel underground stone refuge, an adult woman slightly lifts one ceiling stone and a narrow sheet of water enters. Other family members retreat toward the lower level. No drowning body, no machinery, no pyramid. Rooms separated by physically cut stone-colored paper.
myths.huella: A short totumo branch supporting a small bird and a tail-hanging opossum floats above two broad low layers, one muted blue flood and one warm ochre trace of later fire. One compact balanced motif with ample blank paper.
myths.limits: Different phases are condensed only in the symbolic third piece. No generic mountain river, ark or sunken human bodies. Owl transformation and later rebuilding remain in written narrative.

myths.title: Huhum, el sapo que trajo el fuego
myths.entrada: Two Ette adult women place uncooked food on a sun-warmed stone beside their lowland settlement. Far across the Gran Río a tiny enemy-bank hearth has a warm ember. No fire in their own settlement yet.
myths.acto: At night the large Mamu toad has crossed back over the Gran Río and spits exactly one small ember safely onto dry ground before waiting Ette adults. Toad remains an animal, no human arms, no burning creature. Broad cut-paper water planes, tiny warm fire.
myths.huella: A single natural squat toad silhouette with one small warm ember just before its mouth, supported by a short blue river-paper strip. Cream negative space. Ember is cut paper, not glowing digital magic.
myths.limits: Huhum becomes Mamu and REMAINS a toad; no later human return, no fire ritual or enemy combat.

myths.title: La ceiba que guardaba el maíz
myths.entrada: Ette adults labor with simple cutting tools at the base of a tall ceiba in daylight. A small maize cob with seeds is caught at its upper branches. Wide lowland forest clearing and small full-body figures.
myths.acto: The same community continues cutting the same giant ceiba through the night, a pale small midnight moon high above. The tree tilts gently toward a cleared empty side after prolonged labor; nobody underneath, no injury. Seed-bearing upper branches remain visible.
myths.huella: A single maize cob and a few kernels emerging from an irregular cut ceiba cross-section, with one small plain moon arc above. Earthy compact assemblage on blank warm paper.
myths.limits: Not stolen maize from Aruacos. No evil tree deity or instant magic felling. Moon is editorial time cue, not a cultural sign.

myths.title: La semilla guardada durante el gran verano
myths.entrada: In a dry failed roza, one adult opens a plain fique reserve bag containing only a few maize seeds, while two others look on. Hot cracked soil, no lush crops yet. Pale dusty air and muted ochres.
myths.acto: After the rains return, two Ette adults plant the few saved maize kernels ON a fallen moisture-holding log, not directly in the still-hot dry soil. One small first shoot emerges from the log; no miraculous full cornfield.
myths.huella: A short fallen log of flat bark-paper layers holding a few maize kernels and one modest green shoot. The log visibly supports the roots above a thin hot-soil layer. Cream empty field.
myths.limits: Collective recovery, not a deity rewarding a hero. Fique bag here, distinct from the small cotton-seed bag in myth355.

myths.title: La semilla de algodón compartida
myths.entrada: An Ette adult host stands in the doorway of a modest lowland house; an adult Aruaco visitor stands outside requesting a few cotton seeds. Plain unadorned historical garments, no invented distinctive Aruaco insignia. Cautious separated body language.
myths.acto: The Ette host places a FEW cotton seeds in the open palm of the adult visitor beside the house doorway. An intimate concrete exchange, only two adults, no crowds, treaty, banquet or embrace symbolizing universal peace.
myths.huella: Two small open cut-paper palms separated by a narrow gap with a few cotton seeds crossing it and one modest cotton boll behind them. Compact tactile motif, pale cream surrounding.
myths.limits: Do not infer a universal reconciliation or new named characters. Hands and boll are an editorial metaphor for sharing.

myths.title: El palo que abrió el agua
myths.entrada: An adult father and his THREE adult sons stand around a deeply planted plain stick in a forest opening. The first son pulls and fails; the second and third wait. No rivalry or crowns. Father is not a shaman.
myths.acto: The THIRD adult son lifts the single stick clear of its hole and a broad fresh water jet immediately rises from the opening. Father and two other sons watch from a safe distance. Exactly four people, no river magically formed.
myths.huella: One straight wooden stick raised over a small earth aperture with a single broad blue cut-paper water spout. Much blank cream around this compact gesture.
myths.limits: No botanical species assigned, no secret inherited ritual, distinct from the Cacica saliva myth.

myths.title: La llamada «mala mujer»
myths.entrada: An elderly frail adult man rests in shade beside the roza while his adult wife stands at a respectful distance asking him to work. His two adult sons are small figures departing toward the forest to hunt tapir. No attack, no stereotyped evil facial expression.
myths.acto: Two adult sons encounter their deceased father appearing upright in a clean forest clearing. He now has the specifically narrated festive achiote skin color, threads at ankles knees and arms, NEW skirt, chest ribbon, a modest yellow/red feather crown, small macaw-tail feathers, bow, arrows and macana. Broad cut-paper wind sheets partly obscure him. No skeleton, no ghost glow, no killing of the mother.
myths.huella: An abandoned macana crossed by a broad wind-cut paper gap and one small red/yellow feather pair. Compact memorial-like editorial motif without crown, victory or bloody weapon.
myths.limits: Festive feather attire is allowed ONLY here because this narrative explicitly describes it; not a generic Chimila uniform. Do not present matricide as justice; violent outcome remains in attributed text, not image.

myths.title: La casa de los muertos en el monte
myths.entrada: A lone adult traveler lost in the forest reaches a modest house in a cleared patch. It looks ordinary, not haunted or ruined; wide foliage opening and spacious framing.
myths.acto: Inside the modest house, several dead residents sit naturally on the floor and answer the living visitor, who stands startled near the open exit. Normal human paper-cut bodies, no wounds, skeletons, floating ghosts or captions. Their language is represented only by separated opposed broad paper sound shapes that do not meet.
myths.huella: A plain house doorway bisected by a thin empty paper gap, with two short groups of broad conversation arcs on opposing sides that do not join. Blank warm cream around the compact symbol.
myths.limits: The dead speak, they do NOT stay silent or pursue him. Sound arcs are editorial notation, not writing or authentic ritual glyphs.

myths.title: Los buenos y los malos brujos
myths.entrada: Three adult travelers stop at a round house at nightfall. Two remain outside warning the third as he approaches the dark doorway. No occult symbols, no monstrous decoration, no weapon combat.
myths.acto: A large NATURAL jaguar appears just outside the round house at night; the two adults who stayed outside flee in the far forest opening. No body shown in the house, no attack or bloody mouth. The uncertainty between animal and returning dead is kept, not literal hybrid man-cat.
myths.huella: A natural jaguar's cut-paper profile overlaps a small empty round-house doorway and its dark inner absence. One compact quiet ambiguous motif, no monster fangs or magic eyes.
myths.limits: Not all jaguars are witches. No destruction ritual or invented witch regalia. Death represented by absence, not corpse.

myths.title: El crimen ocultado
myths.entrada: A modest Ette village gathering with chicha in plain vessels and small groups of adults drinking and dancing; two adult men leave toward the forest as night falls. No carnivorous feast or stereotypes.
myths.acto: Two adult perpetrators stand separately on a now-empty dark forest path, a lowered macana between them, looking back toward the distant village. The third man is absent; restrained uneasy stillness, no body, no blood, no consumption, no roasting or meat.
myths.huella: One plain lowered macana beside a interrupted path and an empty third footprint position suggested by a clean cut-out gap. Pale quiet background, no fire or food.
myths.limits: This is an individual crime concealed from the cacique, NOT an ethnic custom. No confession, punishment or justice invented; no cannibalism depicted.

myths.title: La enfermedad después de la guerra
myths.entrada: A small adult Ette armed group leaves toward the Gran Río, with bows held at their sides. Vast river and opposing bank in the background. No children or combat targets.
myths.acto: An adult who returned from the war sits fatigued near his lowland house, two adult companions watching quietly at a distance. No wound, medical rash, dead children, doctor, cure or repentance scene.
myths.huella: Two equal empty human-shaped paper shadows separated by one broad Gran Río strip, each beside one lowered bow. Compact paired absence on cream paper.
myths.limits: Correspondence of losses is an attributed narrative relation, not verified medical cause, moral justice or a second battle. Empty shadows are editorial metaphor.

myths.title: Los animales hablan
myths.entrada: A natural tapir in an open forest patch calls toward other animals to share ordinary food, a few fallen leaves and edible natural plant matter. Small monkeys are visible high in distant branches. No bowls or human clothes.
myths.acto: Two natural monkeys in separate forest branches face each other and answer in the morning; tapir visible small below. Ordinary animal communication, no human lips or hands in prayer, no council or speech text.
myths.huella: Two natural monkey head profiles face each other across a small empty gap with two broad simple cut-paper sound arcs between them. One short branch base, extensive pale blank area.
myths.limits: Animals speak as an ordinary capacity in the tale; no invented animal assembly or magical glowing aura. Arcs are editorial convention.

myths.title: El mono que devolvió la flecha
myths.entrada: A lone adult hunter watches a monkey high in the forest canopy at morning. His bow is held ready but no arrow hits anything. Full-body person small against broad tree layers.
myths.acto: The monkey holds the SAME missed straight arrow it picked up, about to return it toward the hunter hiding behind a thick tree trunk. No impact or injured person. Natural monkey proportions, no costume.
myths.huella: Exactly one straight arrow held by a natural monkey paw silhouette; its paper shadow points in the opposite direction across one leaf. A compact return motif on cream without any human body.
myths.limits: One actual arrow, not two arrows or a victory battle. Human death remains in narrative; the image stops before impact.

myths.title: El hombre que soñó con una danta
myths.entrada: A sleeping adult man in his modest shelter has a clearly separated inset-like dream layer of a fallen forest trunk beside a tapir. Two realities distinguished by a clean paper gap, not blended into a real tapir beside his bed. No crushed body or meal.
myths.acto: The awakened adult traveler walks alone in the forest as strong wind bends branches and a huge trunk begins to fall across the open route ahead. No tree impact, no corpse, no attacking tapir. Lots of tall forest air.
myths.huella: A single fallen log casting two offset flat cut-paper shadows, one suggesting a tapir and the other a small human footprint, not a body. Large cream field around it.
myths.limits: Dream and waking outcome are inverted. Do not assign demonic causation to the tapir or show the later slaughter. Shadow is editorial metaphor.

myths.title: El hombre que soñó con un caimán
myths.entrada: Two adult brothers arrive at a Gran Río fishing beach; one hesitant, one inviting. A natural large caiman lies partly in distant water. No egg physically eaten here, no attack. Wide quiet beach and distant banks.
myths.acto: The natural caiman's mouth is OPEN, held apart by ONE straight arrow wedged between its jaws. A small adult man steps OUT through the opening to safety on the riverbank; no crushing, blood, damaged animal interior or extra arrows piercing skin. Clear escape silhouette.
myths.huella: An open natural caiman-jaw cutout held apart by one straight arrow, with two broad low sound arcs beyond it alluding to the later learned whistle. Compact motif on cream, no bloody teeth or heroic trophy.
myths.limits: Later recovery and whistling are not an instant reward; symbol condenses escape and subsequent learning. No cannibal scene.

myths.title: El morrocoyo que antes era gente
myths.entrada: The BEFORE-shell morrocoy is a small natural turtle-like animal with NO shell perched in a tree; two adult hunters below hesitate at recognizing its people-like former condition. Natural animal without human face or clothing, no arrow wound.
myths.acto: Beside a creek, the transformed natural morrocoy now carries a shell whose broad layered plates visibly echo tree bark. No hands making armor, no ritual, no hunters killing or cooking it.
myths.huella: A compact natural morrocoy silhouette whose shell is made of overlapping broad flat bark-paper plates, with one small blue creek strip below. No face, arrow or cooking vessel, ample cream blank space.
myths.limits: Before-shell entry versus bark-shell ending. No Wuacha, Jacinto or other invented named characters. Intermediate killings omitted visually.

myths.title: Yunari y las cinco tierras
myths.entrada: Yunari the ancient female Earth Mother is a small mature woman integrated into broad earth layers and branching waterways, the landscape gently echoing her body without nudity or literal blood. Human land relationship, not a carved giant goddess statue. Muted wide sky.
myths.acto: Show two occupied flat earth levels separated in tall open space: current fourth Middle Earth below under daylight, future fifth Ette Kooronda above under night, with its people as thick-paper silhouettes, not soldiers in invented armor. The upper plane gently descends, no disaster or falling bodies.
myths.huella: Exactly FIVE broad horizontal earth-paper layers as one compact stack. The fourth is subtly supported by two simple earth-colored pillars; the fifth sits above, thin blue water/darkness below the stack. Cream negative space.
myths.limits: Five earths are not planets. Pillars and body-territory are editorial spatial visualization of narrative concepts, not an authenticated traditional diagram. No certain apocalypse timetable.

myths.title: Yaau, Numirinta y las dos mazorcas
myths.entrada: Male Yaau and female Numirinta stand on opposite edges of the San Ángel savanna lagoon, looking toward East and West respectively. Equal visual importance, two complementary adult creators, small full figures in a wide landscape.
myths.acto: Yaau and Numirinta bring exactly TWO cariaco maize cobs together beside the lagoon; small new adult human cutouts emerge as an abstract row from their kernels, non-biological creation, no infants, wombs or medical imagery. Both creators act equally.
myths.huella: Exactly TWO maize cobs mirrored toward complementary directions, a few kernels becoming tiny simple human footprint cut-outs below. Warm cream surrounding, no yin-yang sign or invented tribal glyph.
myths.limits: This is the contemporary maize version, NOT Papá Grande's clay or the falling first man. Footprints are an editorial metaphor.
